title: Optimization Campaign Report
description: report.json (design spec 3.6, 3.9) -- the end of a kind:optimization campaign: the recommended configuration, WHICH RUNG of the fallback ladder produced it, and the residual-regret certificate. Written by orchestrator.optimize.stage_runner._run_report at the compiled epoch's `report` state AND on the way out of a semantic exception, so every field must be expressible when the strongest rungs were unavailable. THE TWO REGRET BOUNDS ARE NEVER COLLAPSED (design spec 3.5): residual_regret_model and residual_regret_terminal are separate, independently required, independently nullable properties, and this schema declares no relationship, default, or derived combination between them -- collapsing them would advertise the assumption-light terminal guarantee while delivering the model-dependent one. There is deliberately no combined-regret property to add a value to.

recommendation.description: The configuration the campaign returns. ALWAYS PRESENT: a finite-budget system that cannot certify must still act (design spec 3.6), so this object exists even when every rung above `none` was unavailable.

levels.description: The recommended factor levels. Empty ONLY under basis `none`, where no legal configuration existed to return.

basis.description: Which rung of the fallback ladder (design spec 3.6) produced this recommendation, strongest first. certified: terminal discrimination ran and R_terminal <= epsilon. terminal_best: terminal discrimination ran but the bound was too wide -- still a measured winner against measured rivals. model: no terminal stage ran; the fitted argmax stands on its model bound, and this is the ONE rung suppressed when epoch_ended is present, because a semantic exception is evidence against the fitted surface. measured: the best measured VALID configuration (complete rows only, never the largest noisy observation). baseline: the author's known_valid_baseline. none: NOT a rung -- no baseline was declared and nothing else survived, so there is genuinely nothing legal to return. A reader must be able to tell a certificate from a fallback without reading the log, which is why this enum is closed.

value.description: The recommended configuration's objective value: the confirmed mean under certified/terminal_best, the model's prediction under `model`, the measurement under `measured`. ABSENT (not null) under `baseline` and `none`, where no value is known -- _run_report only includes the key when the value is not None, so a reader can distinguish `no value known` from `a value of null`.

residual_regret_model.description: R_delta(x) from the FITTED surface at delta_screen (design spec 3.5), copied from the latest recommendation.json's residual_regret_model.value. Rests on the registered response class. It is the bound AT THE FITTED ARGMAX (recommendation.json.levels), which may differ from recommendation.levels here -- a fallback rung can recommend a different configuration -- and it is not a bound on the recommendation when the fit was judged inadequate. Null when no fitting stage ran, or when the bound was not computable (pure error exactly zero). SEPARATE FROM residual_regret_terminal BY CONSTRUCTION: the two rest on different assumptions and are computed from disjoint inputs (fitted coefficients and their standard errors vs finalist sample means and variances), so one is never the other under a different key.

residual_regret_terminal.description: R_delta(x) from TERMINAL DISCRIMINATION at delta_terminal (design spec 3.5), copied from the latest confirmation.json. Carries nothing but the fresh measurements of the realized shortlist -- no response model. Null when no confirm state ran, when no finalist produced a valid measurement, when the bound was not estimable, or when any admissible finalist went unmeasured (an unknown rival makes the max unknown, and an unknown is not a zero; confirmation.json's terminal_bound_measured_only keeps the survivors-only number). SEPARATE FROM residual_regret_model BY CONSTRUCTION; see that property.

epsilon.description: The resolved epsilon-optimality tolerance the bounds are compared against, from confirmation.json when a terminal stage ran, else from recommendation.json. Null when neither exists (e.g. an exception ended the epoch before any fit).

epsilon_reference.description: Copied from confirmation.json's epsilon_reference: which reference a percentage epsilon was resolved against (best_finalist / best_observed / recommendation / declared_abs / none). Null when no terminal stage ran (epsilon then comes from recommendation.json).

delta_screen.description: The screening risk from the compiled policy's objective. Reported next to residual_regret_model because a bound without its delta is not a bound. The two deltas are what Pr(wrong global decision) <= delta_screen + delta_terminal sums, and keeping them apart here is the report-level half of the 3.5 obligation.

delta_terminal.description: The terminal-discrimination risk from the compiled policy's objective, the delta residual_regret_terminal is stated at.

certified.description: True only when terminal discrimination ran AND certified globally. A bound at or below epsilon is NOT enough: an inadmissible or unmeasured finalist, a fit whose exclusions were level-correlated, or a fitting stage whose lack-of-fit test rejected the model (model_inadequate), withholds certification -- certification_withheld names which.

certification_withheld.description: Why `certified` is false, so the report never pairs an unexplained `certified: false` with bounds that look as though they should certify. Empty exactly when certified is true. Copied from the latest confirmation.json's certification_withheld (see confirmation.schema.json for each reason); `no_terminal_discrimination` when no confirm state ran, so no certificate was attempted. `reason_not_recorded` when the confirmation.json it reads predates the reasons field. `no_admissible_finalist` when every finalist was measured inadmissible (see confirmation.schema.json). `model_inadequate` when the shortlist rests on a fit the lack-of-fit test rejected (see confirmation.schema.json). Optional here only so reports written before the field existed still validate; _run_report always writes it.

finalists.description: The realized terminal shortlist carried forward from confirmation.json, each entry as written there. Empty when no confirm state ran.

known_valid_baseline.description: The author's declared known-good configuration, from the compiled policy. Null when none was declared -- which is exactly what makes basis `none` reachable.

path.description: The states this EPOCH passed through, read back from transitions.jsonl scoped to this epoch (policy.epoch_transitions). Epoch-scoped deliberately: an unfiltered read would splice a previous epoch's rows in and name a transition this epoch never made.

epoch.description: Which compiled epoch this report describes. A semantic exception ends an epoch; a recompilation from a revised campaign starts the next one.

epoch_ended.description: GENUINELY OPTIONAL, not nullable: _run_report includes this key ONLY when a semantic exception ended the epoch, and its value is the guard that fired (state plus the `when` clause). Its mere PRESENCE is the signal -- a reader can tell an ordinary report from one written on the way out of a failed epoch without reading the log, and epoch_end-<epoch>.json carries the full record next to it. Its presence also suppresses the `model` rung of the ladder.

candidate_space.description: GENUINELY OPTIONAL: present exactly when the recommendation.json residual_regret_model is copied from had a candidate_space, i.e. its candidate space was SEARCHED rather than enumerated (above decide.CANDIDATE_CAP). A verbatim copy of that record, so a reader of report.json alone knows the model bound and the fitted argmax are over the search's evaluated set, not a proven optimum over X_valid (INV-STAT18). Absent means that space was enumerated exactly.

exhaustive.description: Always false when present: the evaluated set is a subset of the space.

size.description: The product of the fitted factors' axis sizes: the full candidate space, before exclusions.

evaluated.description: Distinct configurations the search scored (before measured-inadmissible and confidently-infeasible exclusions).

seed.description: The search seed (decide.SEARCH_SEED): the same fit and exclusions always reproduce the same evaluated set.

constraint_models_applied.description: Whether confidently-infeasible candidates were excluded. null: no constraint was modelled. true: applied at every evaluated point. false: dropped because neither the search nor a feasibility-seeking descent (on the total constraint violation, the hinge sum of the per-constraint margins) found an admissible point -- the searched analogue of the enumerated rule 'drop only when the whole space is confidently infeasible'. constraint_models[].applied agrees with it, and constraint_models[].excluded_confidently_infeasible counts over the evaluated set.

boundary_optimum.description: GENUINELY OPTIONAL: present only when refine's fitted optimum lay OUTSIDE the declared ranges and the policy's registered boundary branch (optimization.policy.out_of_hull: confirm, the default) confirmed the best configuration inside them. Any certificate in this report is scoped to the declared ranges; `axes` are the factors whose stationary coordinate lay past [-1, 1] -- widen them (report.md says to what) unless the edge is a hard limit of the system.

held_out.description: GENUINELY OPTIONAL: present only when response.held_out is declared. The generalization check, READ after every decision in this report was made and fed to none of them (orchestrator/optimize/held_out.py). For the recommendation and each finalist: the held-out metric's mean over this epoch's complete rows at exactly those levels, and the primary metric's mean over the SAME rows, so the two are compared on equal footing. n = 0 means no complete row measured that configuration -- not a zero.

pareto.description: Multi-objective campaigns only (spec 2026-10-15-pareto-front-design.md steps 5-8): the MEASURED front over every admissible configuration the campaign measured (confirm finalists and fitting-stage rows, means over complete rows), each point's dominance status, the preferred point, the hypervolume and the remaining gaps.

front.description: Points no other measured point eps-dominates in point estimate, sorted best-first by the first objective. `confidently_nondominated`: for EVERY other measured point some objective's one-sided upper bound on its advantage is below that objective's epsilon (pooled pure-error variance, Bonferroni over rivals x objectives at delta_front), and no adequate-model prediction beats it by epsilon on every objective. Otherwise `possibly_dominated`, and `dominated_by` names who could not be ruled out.

value.description: null (with `reason`) when no point is confidently_nondominated: undefined, not zero.

gap_threshold.description: null when no objective's epsilon is known: no gap can be called large.

epsilon_unknown.description: Objectives whose epsilon has no reference (null in `epsilon`); certification is withheld (epsilon_unknown).

predicted_rivals.description: Whether predicted-front candidates were checked as rivals of measured points (only when every objective model is adequate).

excluded_incomplete.description: Measured admissible configurations left out of the front because a complete row lacked a usable value for some objective (missing, null, NaN or non-numeric). A confirm finalist among them is unmeasured and blocks certification.

certification_caveats.description: Facts that weaken the certificate's premise without withholding it. Present only when non-empty. `finalist_measured_infeasible`: a finalist was measured inadmissible but at least two admissible finalists remained, their simultaneous bound is within epsilon and the model was adequate (stage_runner._INFEASIBLE_FINALIST_CAVEAT).

policy_hash.description: Content hash of the compiled policy this epoch ran under -- the pre-registration this report is accountable to. Joins to transitions.jsonl's rows and to policy.sha256.

iteration.description: The iteration index at which the report was written. May be LATER than the confirm it describes (a budget-exhausted route to `report`, or a resumed work_dir), which is why the terminal rungs read confirmation.json off disk rather than trusting a threaded argument.
